evidence.quote: let renewalRefusal (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : LendingError option =
NotRenewable = Loans.renewalRefusal today loan library |> Option.map (renewalReason loan) }
let renewAll (today: DateOnly) memberId (library: Library) : Result<Library * (Loan * Result<Loan, LendingError>) list, LendingError> =
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-01.rationale: (Line numbers are line numbers in the patch file.) The renewal rule (overdue first, then the limit, then holds, in that order) sits in one Tier 2 function, renewalRefusal. Both Loans.renew and the new Loans.renewAll call it. Tier 3 (Views.ofLoan) asks Tier 2 whether a loan can be renewed and only turns the LendingError it gets back into the listing wording (renewalReason). It does not test for overdue, the limit or holds itself. renew-all's ordering and per-loan outcomes are also decided in Tier 2. The change also removes the CLI's old direct call to Loans.renew, so the CLI now goes through UseCases.renew. Tier 3's Renewed/Total counts and the CLI's empty-list message are only presentation of results Tier 2 already decided.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect was added below Tier 4. Today's date reaches the code through the Clock port in Tier 3 (UseCases.loans, and commit for renew/renewAll) and is passed as a value into pure Tier 2 and view code. Saving goes through the existing commit/Store port. The change removes an older bypass in which the CLI loaded and saved the store and called Loans.renew directly from Tier 4, so presentation no longer re-enters Tier 2. Loans.renewAll is pure (a mapFold over Library), so it can be tested without effects.

evidence.quote: elif loan.Renewals >= Policy.renewLimit then Some(RenewLimitReached(loan.Copy, Policy.renewLimit))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Every use refers to the one definition, Policy.renewLimit: the guard, the RenewView limit, and the reason text, which takes the limit from the error value. No literal 2 is repeated in production code. The three renewal conditions were moved out of renew's inline ensure chain into renewalRefusal, so loans and renew cannot disagree. The loan period and due-date arithmetic stay in the existing Tier 2 renew.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: (Line numbers are line numbers in the patch file.) The rule that the limit depends on member type is written in Tier 2: Policy.renewLimit maps member type to limit, and Loans.renewLimitOf finds the borrower's limit, including the fallback when the borrower is missing. renewalRefusal uses it. Tier 3 asks Loans.renewLimitOf for the number it shows and does not work out the member type or the limit itself. The CLI and persistence code are unchanged.

evidence.quote: |> Result.map (fun (l, loan) -> l, Views.ofRenew l loan))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effects. The change only passes the in-memory Library value further into the pure view projection, and Tier 2's renewLimitOf is a pure lookup. The clock and the store are still reached through the existing ports and commit.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The per-type limits (2/1/4) are defined only in Policy.renewLimit. The guard, the RenewLimitReached payload, which feeds the 'renewed X of Y times' text, and the renewal-count display all get the limit from the single Loans.renewLimitOf. No copy of the old single limit is left behind. The decision document is updated to match the code.
